consensus_summary: Babel/Babylon is the archetypal symbol of human pride, self-exaltation, and organized rebellion against God—the idolatrous, oppressive ‘city of man’ or anti-God world system/empire destined for judgment, set against the city of God.
book_summary: The self-made kingdom that builds a name against heaven—an empire raised over many kingdoms, the covenant counterfeit.
consensus_core_identification: Prideful human rebellion forming an idolatrous anti-God empire/world-system (city of man).
book_core_identification: Self-made kingdom building a name against heaven; multi-kingdom empire that is the covenant counterfeit.
boundary_disagreement: Book preserves the anti-God self-exalting kingdom/empire but tightens the identification to a covenant counterfeit (false covenant kingdom) and an empire raised over many kingdoms, rather than the broader consensus category of any prideful world-system or city-of-man.
rationale: Minimum cores share the same referent (Babel’s name-building rebellion extended as Babylonian anti-God empire). The book does not replace that referent; it adds precision and a narrowing condition (‘covenant counterfeit,’ empire-over-kingdoms) that selects a tighter theological boundary inside the consensus category. Differences are therefore refinement of extension/precision, not contradiction or novelty.
strongest_objection: ‘Covenant counterfeit’ is not an explicit primary consensus gloss and could be read as importing a more specific ecclesial/theological frame than the cited verses alone require.
